I need to build a knowledge base from recent papers about large language model fine-tuning and alignment. Please access our academic paper repository and read the full content of papers that are relevant to the topics of LLM fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture improvements. For each relevant paper, read through its sections carefully to understand the methodology and key results. Skip any papers that are about unrelated topics like robotics or physical systems.

Create a Notion page titled LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base. The page should contain blocks for each relevant paper, where each block covers the paper title, the key method introduced, and the main findings from the paper.

Also create a Word document called LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx in my workspace. The document should start with a heading called LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey, followed by an introduction paragraph. Then include a dedicated section for each relevant paper that presents the paper title, the author names, a description of the method, and the key results extracted from reading the paper sections.

Finally, create a Google Sheet called LLM Paper Registry with columns for ArXiv_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Date, Key_Contribution, and Method_Category, with one row per relevant paper.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent itself runs the compact discovery queries, then uses one parallel full-text reader wave of three per-paper explorers and one parallel writer wave of three deliverable owners.

Before Wave 1, the main agent covers the task-relevant local arXiv candidate space in read-only mode through complementary fine-tuning, alignment, and architecture queries at the supported per-call bound; unions and deduplicates all returned IDs (the search exposes no cursor); applies the task's relevance rule (reject robotics or physical-system distractors); and freezes exactly three retained paper IDs — never importing outside facts or importing rejected IDs downstream.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per retained paper ID:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Reader for retained paper 1. Use the local repository read_paper tool with paper_id = that literal assigned ID, read through ALL sections of the paper (not just the abstract) to understand the methodology and key results, and return EXACTLY the structured report {paper_id, title, full authors, published date, key method, source-backed findings, method category, section coverage}. Read-only: do not create Notion, Word, Google Sheet, or intermediate files.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Reader for retained paper 2 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Reader for retained paper 3 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies one handoff per retained ID, deduplicates titles, verifies every rejected paper against the exclusion rule, and freezes one normalized packet with per-paper controls.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own the single Notion page exclusively. Search for LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base, create at most one page, add one substantive block per frozen paper with title, method, and findings, and read it back. Return page ID/title, paper coverage, block count, and validation. Do not write the Word document or Google Sheet.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx exclusively. Create it exactly once with the required heading, introduction, and one author/method/results section for every frozen paper. Read it back and return path, headings, retained-paper coverage, and validation. Do not modify Notion or Google Sheets.
3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Use one coder sub-agent to own the Google Sheet LLM Paper Registry exclusively. Create it once with the exact six columns and one row per frozen paper, preserving full authors and source dates and using controlled Method_Category values. Read it back and return spreadsheet/sheet IDs, headers, row count, and validation. Do not write Notion or Word state.

After Wave 2, the main agent must reconcile the same stable-ID set, authors, methods, and findings across all deliverables, verify every rejected paper appears nowhere, and complete only after file and external-state checks. Do not dispatch any further agent and do not add a verification wave.

We are building a knowledge base about LLM fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture improvements. Your job: read ONE arXiv paper IN FULL and report a structured, factual extraction of its contents.

The paper's arXiv ID is 2305.20050. It is already downloaded in our local paper repository. Read it with the tool `mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper` passing paper_id="2305.20050" (full markdown content). Read through ALL sections carefully, including abstract, method/approach sections, experiments, and results. If some content appears truncated or you need more precision on math/pipeline details, you may additionally use `mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_prompt` with arxiv_id="2305.20050" or `mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_section` with arxiv_id="2305.20050" and a section path found via `mcp__arxiv-latex__list_paper_sections`.

Report back the following, clearly labelled:
1. FULL TITLE (exact).
2. AUTHORS: the complete ordered list of author names as found in the paper content. If the paper body does not list authors, state that explicitly.
3. PUBLISHED DATE: the paper's arXiv submission/publication date if present in the content (state it explicitly if absent).
4. KEY METHOD: the name and a precise 3-6 sentence description of the main method/technique/architecture introduced — what it is, how it works, what problem it solves, and its core mechanism (e.g., loss formulation, training pipeline stages, architectural components like attention variants).
5. METHODOLOGY DETAILS: models/scale, training data or datasets, training procedure, and evaluation benchmarks used.
6. MAIN FINDINGS / KEY RESULTS: the important quantitative results (exact benchmark numbers, percentages, parameter counts, comparisons vs. baselines) and the qualitative conclusions the authors draw.
7. METHOD_CATEGORY: one concise category label classifying the paper's method (e.g., "Preference Alignment", "RLHF / Preference Optimization", "Supervised Fine-Tuning & RLHF Pipeline", "Model Architecture Improvement", "Efficient Attention Architecture"). Choose the single best label.
8. KEY_CONTRIBUTION: one single sentence (<= 40 words) summarizing the paper's contribution for a registry row.

Be strictly factual — only report what the paper actually states, and keep exact numbers. If a piece of information is absent, write "not stated". Your final message should be the structured report only.
Read 3 LLM papers in depth

GOAL: Create a Notion page titled "LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base" (a top-level page in the workspace) and populate it with the structured content specified below. Then verify it exists and report back.

CONTEXT / DIAGNOSTICS (read carefully, this is important):
- The Notion workspace is currently EMPTY: mcp__notion__API-post-search with an empty query returns no results. So the new page must be created as a top-level page (parent = workspace).
- The main agent already tried repeatedly to create the page with mcp__notion__API-post-page and every attempt failed with this exact validation error:
  Invalid args for tool "mcp__notion__API-post-page": /parent must be object; /parent must be object; /parent must be object; /parent must match exactly one schema in oneOf; /properties must be object
  Attempts already tried and failed (all produced that identical error):
    * parent={"workspace": true}, properties={"title":[{"text":{"content":"LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base"}}]}
    * parent={"type":"workspace","workspace":true}
    * parent={"type":"page_id","page_id":"12345678-1234-4a12-8a34-123456789012"}
    * passing both params as JSON-encoded strings
  A related tool, mcp__notion__API-patch-page with a "properties" object, fails with "/properties must be object".
  IMPORTANT CLUE: object parameters whose schema declares an explicit "type": "object" DO work — e.g. mcp__notion__API-create-a-comment with parent={"page_id":"..."} succeeded. Only parameters whose schema is a bare "$ref" (parent/properties on post-page and patch-page) fail. It looks like $ref-typed params arrive at the server as strings instead of objects.
- Your job is to find a working way to create the page despite this. Ideas to try (in roughly this order, and feel free to invent others):
  1. mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent and properties supplied as JSON-encoded strings (parameter value written as a quoted JSON string).
  2. mcp__notion__API-post-page with properties as a legacy simplified title array, e.g. properties=["LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base"].
  3. mcp__notion__API-post-page with a minimal properties object.
  4. Any other encoding variation you can think of (different key orders, minimal whitespace, "Name" instead of "title", etc.).
  5. If a page gets created but is missing blocks, use mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children (its "children" array parameter works fine) to append the remaining blocks.
- Keep trying until the page exists with its content, or until you have exhausted reasonable options. Do not give up after one failure. Report the exact outcome of each attempt.

PAGE TITLE: LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base

PAGE CONTENT — create exactly these blocks, in this order:

BLOCK 1 — paragraph:
This knowledge base summarises recent papers from our academic paper repository covering large language model fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture improvements. Three papers met the relevance criteria and are documented below. The repository's robotics paper (Robot Learning with Affordances) was reviewed and excluded as out of scope.

BLOCK 2 — heading level 2:
1. Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model (arXiv:2305.20050)

BLOCK 3 — paragraph:
Authors: Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma | Published: 2023-05-30 | Method Category: Preference Alignment

BLOCK 4 — heading level 3:
Key Method: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)

BLOCK 5 — paragraph:
DPO is a stable, performant and computationally lightweight alternative to RLHF that directly optimizes the language model policy. Instead of the conventional two-stage pipeline that first fits an explicit reward model to preference data and then optimises the policy against it with reinforcement learning such as PPO, DPO reparameterizes the reward function in terms of the policy itself: the reward of a response is expressed through the ratio of the fine-tuned policy's probability to that of a fixed reference (SFT) policy. This closed-form relationship turns the constrained reward-maximisation objective into a simple classification-style loss applied to pairs of preferred and dispreferred responses, so the policy is optimised directly on preference data with no separate reward model and no RL sampling loop.

BLOCK 6 — heading level 3:
Main Findings

BLOCK 7 — three bulleted list items:
- DPO aligns language models to human preferences without explicit reward modeling, removing both the reward-model training stage and the reinforcement learning loop of standard RLHF.
- The method is reported to be stable, performant and computationally lightweight, making preference alignment simpler and cheaper to run than PPO-based RLHF.
- Because the language model itself acts as the reward model (the model is 'secretly a reward model'), the same network supplies both the policy and the preference signal, simplifying the alignment pipeline.

BLOCK 8 — heading level 2:
2. Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models (arXiv:2307.09288)

BLOCK 9 — paragraph:
Authors: Hugo Touvron, Louis Martin | Published: 2023-07-18 | Method Category: Supervised Fine-Tuning and RLHF

BLOCK 10 — heading level 3:
Key Method: Pretrained foundation models plus a dialogue fine-tuning pipeline (Llama 2-Chat)

BLOCK 11 — paragraph:
The paper develops and releases Llama 2, a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned large language models ranging in scale from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters. The method is a staged fine-tuning recipe for dialogue: large-scale pretraining of a decoder-only transformer family is followed by supervised fine-tuning on curated instruction and dialogue data, and then reinforcement learning from human feedback in which a reward model is trained on human preference comparisons and used to iteratively refine the policy. The resulting aligned models, released openly as Llama 2-Chat, are optimised for dialogue use cases.

BLOCK 12 — heading level 3:
Main Findings

BLOCK 13 — three bulleted list items:
- The paper delivers an open collection of pretrained and fine-tuned LLMs spanning 7B to 70B parameters, providing both base foundation models and chat-ready variants.
- The fine-tuned Llama 2-Chat models are optimised for dialogue use cases, showing that a supervised fine-tuning plus RLHF pipeline converts a pretrained foundation model into a capable conversational assistant.
- Fine-tuning, rather than further pretraining, is the stage responsible for dialogue behaviour, with the same underlying architecture serving both the base and the aligned chat models.

BLOCK 14 — heading level 2:
3. Mistral 7B (arXiv:2310.06825)

BLOCK 15 — paragraph:
Authors: Albert Jiang, Alexandre Sablayrolles | Published: 2023-10-10 | Method Category: Model Architecture Improvement

BLOCK 16 — heading level 3:
Key Method: Efficiency-focused architecture for a 7-billion-parameter language model

BLOCK 17 — paragraph:
Mistral 7B is a 7-billion-parameter decoder-only language model engineered for superior performance and efficiency. Its gains come from architectural improvements rather than scale: attention design choices such as grouped-query attention and sliding-window attention reduce the memory footprint and the cost of training and inference while preserving the ability to model long contexts. The result is a compact model deliberately designed so that strong capability is achieved with far fewer parameters and less compute than larger open models.

BLOCK 18 — heading level 3:
Main Findings

BLOCK 19 — three bulleted list items:
- Mistral 7B outperforms the best open models of all sizes on all evaluated benchmarks.
- The model demonstrates that architectural improvements can substitute for parameter scale, letting a 7B model match or beat considerably larger open-weight models.
- Superior efficiency is achieved alongside superior performance, making the model a strong compute-effective baseline for fine-tuning and deployment.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA / DELIVERABLE:
- A Notion page titled exactly "LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base" exists, containing blocks for each of the three papers, where each paper's coverage includes the paper title, the key method introduced, and the main findings.
- Verify the result yourself (e.g. mcp__notion__API-post-search for the page, then mcp__notion__API-get-block-children on the page ID to confirm the blocks are present).
- Your final report must state: whether the page was created, the page ID and URL, which approach finally worked (the exact parameter encoding), a list of the block types/text you created, and any leftover issues.

GOAL: Create a Word document named exactly `LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx` in the workspace directory `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-review-notion-word/workspace` (use this absolute path for every Word tool call). Build it with the `mcp__word__*` tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, etc.).

REQUIRED STRUCTURE AND EXACT CONTENT (follow this precisely, in this order):

1. Document title/heading (Heading 1), text exactly: `LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey`
   - Set document metadata: title "LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey", author "LLM Research Assistant".

2. An introduction paragraph (Heading 2 "Introduction" followed by the paragraph, or just the paragraph directly under the main heading — your choice, but the paragraph must be present), text exactly:
`This survey synthesises three recent papers from our academic paper repository that address large language model fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture improvements: Direct Preference Optimization (arXiv:2305.20050), Llama 2 (arXiv:2307.09288), and Mistral 7B (arXiv:2310.06825). Together they cover the three main levers for building capable and aligned language models: a training objective that optimises the policy directly on preference data, a full fine-tuning pipeline that turns a pretrained foundation model into a dialogue assistant, and architectural changes that raise the performance achievable at small scale. A fourth paper in the repository, Robot Learning with Affordances, was reviewed and excluded because it concerns robotics and physical systems rather than language model fine-tuning or alignment. For each included paper, this document records the paper title, the author names, a description of the method, and the key results.`

3. A dedicated section for EACH of the three papers. Each section must contain: the paper title (as a section heading), the author names, a description of the method, and the key results. Use this exact content:

SECTION 1
- Heading 2, text: `1. Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model`
- Paragraph (plain body text): `Authors: Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma | arXiv:2305.20050 | Published: 2023-05-30`
- Heading 3, text: `Method`
- Paragraph:
`Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a stable, performant and computationally lightweight alternative to RLHF that directly optimizes the language model policy. Conventional RLHF first fits an explicit reward model to a dataset of human preference comparisons and then optimises the language model policy against that reward with reinforcement learning such as PPO. DPO removes both stages: it reparameterizes the reward function in terms of the optimal policy, so that the reward of a response is expressed through the ratio of the fine-tuned policy's probability to that of a fixed reference (supervised-fine-tuned) policy. Because this relationship has a closed form, the constrained reward-maximisation objective collapses into a simple classification-style loss applied to pairs of preferred and dispreferred responses, and the policy can be optimised directly on preference data without a separate reward model and without online RL sampling.`
- Heading 3, text: `Key Results`
- Paragraph:
`DPO aligns language models to human preferences without explicit reward modeling and without a reinforcement learning loop, while remaining stable, performant and computationally lightweight relative to standard RLHF. Because the language model itself supplies the preference signal (the model is secretly a reward model), the alignment pipeline is simpler, more stable and cheaper to run than PPO-based approaches.`

SECTION 2
- Heading 2, text: `2. Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models`
- Paragraph (plain body text): `Authors: Hugo Touvron, Louis Martin | arXiv:2307.09288 | Published: 2023-07-18`
- Heading 3, text: `Method`
- Paragraph:
`The paper develops and releases Llama 2, a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned large language models ranging in scale from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters. The method is a staged recipe for producing dialogue-capable models: large-scale pretraining of a decoder-only transformer family, followed by supervised fine-tuning on curated instruction and dialogue data, and then reinforcement learning from human feedback, in which a reward model is trained on human preference comparisons and used to iteratively refine the policy. The resulting aligned models are released openly as Llama 2-Chat.`
- Heading 3, text: `Key Results`
- Paragraph:
`The paper delivers an open collection of pretrained and fine-tuned LLMs spanning 7B to 70B parameters, together with Llama 2-Chat variants that are optimised for dialogue use cases. The results show that the supervised fine-tuning plus RLHF pipeline is what converts a pretrained foundation model into a capable conversational assistant, with the same underlying architecture serving both the base and the aligned chat models.`

SECTION 3
- Heading 2, text: `3. Mistral 7B`
- Paragraph (plain body text): `Authors: Albert Jiang, Alexandre Sablayrolles | arXiv:2310.06825 | Published: 2023-10-10`
- Heading 3, text: `Method`
- Paragraph:
`Mistral 7B is a 7-billion-parameter decoder-only language model engineered for superior performance and efficiency. Its gains come from architectural improvements rather than scale: attention design choices such as grouped-query attention and sliding-window attention reduce the memory footprint and the cost of training and inference while preserving the ability to model long contexts, so that strong capability is achieved with far fewer parameters and much less compute than larger open models.`
- Heading 3, text: `Key Results`
- Paragraph:
`Mistral 7B outperforms the best open models of all sizes on all evaluated benchmarks, showing that architectural improvements can substitute for parameter scale: a compact 7B model matches or beats considerably larger open-weight models while delivering superior efficiency, making it a strong compute-effective baseline for further fine-tuning and deployment.`

CONSTRAINTS:
- Do not add tables, footnotes, images, page breaks, or extra sections beyond what is specified above. Plain headings and paragraphs only.
- Keep the heading text and paragraph text exactly as given (minor whitespace is fine).
- The document must be saved at the absolute path given above and must be a valid .docx.

VERIFICATION AND REPORT:
- After building, verify with `mcp__word__get_document_outline` and `mcp__word__get_document_text` (use the absolute path) and confirm: the document starts with the heading "LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey", the introduction paragraph is present, and all three paper sections with authors, Method and Key Results are present.
- Your final message must state: the absolute file path of the document, the number of headings/paragraphs created, and confirmation from your verification that every required element is present (quote the heading titles you found).
